newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanians beaten in Kuwaiti jail, paper says.
newsitem.headline: Jordanians beaten in Kuwaiti jail, paper says.

text.p: A Jordanian paper said on Wednesday Kuwaiti security men have recently beaten up Jordanians jailed in the emirate since the 1991 Gulf War, sending some to hospital with serious injuries.

The daily Ad-Dustour said a "large number" of Kuwaiti special forces were involved in the attacks in Kuwait's Central Prison where scores of Jordanian and Palestinians are serving long prison sentences on charges of assisting Iraqi forces during their seven-month occupation of Kuwait.
"They hit them severely without interruption which led to a number of them being transferred to hospital where a number of them are being treated for broken bones and injuries," the paper said.
It did not say what prompted the alleged beatings, nor when they took place, but suggested it was in the last few days.
The paper, criticising what it called the silence of the Jordanian government, said its campaign to highlight the plight of Jordanian inmates was in concern for "the dignity of Jordanian citizens".
It called on the government to set up a committee to defend the detainees in Kuwait.
Kuwait's ties with Jordan were strained over its sympathy for Iraq during the seven-month occupation. They continue to be cool despite an improvement in relations with other Gulf states.
